newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - July 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - July 7.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Monday's Daily Variety:
* Sony Corp's Columbia Pictures' "Men in Black" collected an estimated $51 million over the three-day weekend, likely setting a new Independence Day frame record.
* Mimi Leder, who directed DreamWorks' first live-action feature "The Peacemaker," has signed a deal to direct one of her next two features for the company.

* Touchstone Pictures and producer Jerry Bruckheimer won a fevered bidding battle for "Falasha," a fact-based pitch about a Gotham stockbroker drafted by the Mossad to create a Club Med in the Sudan which served as a front for a covert operation to liberate Ethiopian Jews.

* With the breach-of-contract case against John Travolta, who pulled out of the aborted movie project "The Double" last year, headed for trial July 14, lawyers are again asking that perennial Hollywood question: When's a deal a deal?
* More record-shattering bows by The Lost World: Jurassic Park and generally strong preems by Batman & Robin and Con Air kept the foreign box office on the boil last week.

* Screenwriter Ron Bass, who won an Oscar for co-writing "Rain Man," and has a hit on his hands with "My Best Friend's Wedding," has signed a three-year, exclusive writing deal with Sony Pictures Entertainment.
